newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO inch ahead but no Hebron deal.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO inch ahead but no Hebron deal.

text.p: Israel and the Palestinians struggled on Wednesday to sew up a deal on Hebron only hours before Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's scheduled departure on a trip to the United States.
Negotiators resumed marathon talks on Tuesday night with an eye to closing the deal under which Israeli troops would hand over 80 percent of the volatile West Bank town to Palestinian police.
Israeli spokesman Moshe Fogel told reporters in Hebron that Netanyahu, due to speak to Jewish supporters in the United States, would postpone the trip if an agreement was at hand.
Negotiating teams broke for consultations at mid-day.

"We have ended the morning talks but we will continue later in the day. There were still no results because again Israelis are still insisting on hot pursuit rejected by us," Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat told Reuters.
"If Netanyahu gives his negotiators the green light and takes a political decision to stop trying to change the agreement, we will have a deal immediately. We'll see tonight."
Officials said the talks were stalemated over Israel's demand that its forces be allowed to enter PLO-controlled parts of Hebron in "hot pursuit" of suspected attackers.
But Fogel said the sides had achieved "significant progress" and were trying to define how Israeli forces might operate against what he called "terrorists" in Palestinian-run areas.

"They are actually trying to formulate in writing the bounds and limits and ways the Israeli military will be allowed to act in areas of control of the Palestinian Authority," Fogel said of the talks.
Erekat held three hours of intensive talks with Netanyahu's personal adviser, attorney Yitzhak Molho, on Wednesday.
Earlier in the day Netanyahu said he was going ahead with his travel plans. The trip would be his fourth to the United States in five months in power.
"At this stage I haven't changed my trip plans," he told Israel's army radio when asked whether a Hebron accord would be signed on Wednesday.
Netanyahu wants to modify the Hebron deal signed by Israel's previous government to safeguard the 400 Jewish settlers who live and study in guarded enclaves among 100,000 Arabs.
The Hebron pullout was due last March but delayed after Islamist suicide bomb attacks in Israel.
